verdict.reason: The pattern is still observable. In /home/leo/src/reify/.task, plan.json and iterations.jsonl exist, but metadata.json does not. verdict.severity_reason: The cost is real but contained. It shows up as repeated failed invocations and wasted turns in ops sessions, not as a wrong code change, and the fix sits in dark-factory.
verdict.reason: The reify tree has no escalation-watcher skill under .claude/skills, and no script or doc there mentions watcher-rearm.sh or DARK_FACTORY_ROOT. The only hits are the confusion-codebook, census and legibility-test files that record the problem. The codebook (docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml) already holds many sightings of this same confusion: the script missing from reify, then 'DARK_FACTORY_ROOT must be set to a valid directory' (exit 2). So the pattern is recorded as repeating, and the miner's 'novel' label looks wrong. The skill and the script live in dark-factory, outside this tree. The exit-124 ceiling timeouts were not checked against any file here: nothing in this tree runs watcher-rearm.sh, and the timeout cause is unverified.

new.observation: Across these sessions the agent probed .task/ at bootstrap for metadata.json, iterations.jsonl and reviews/ and met repeated not-found errors, with .task/plan.json an absolute symlink into <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<lane>/ that is often dangling. The runbook at the anchor calls the dangling symlink usual and uninteresting but states no contract for which artifacts a lane guarantees, so the bootstrap layout has no single home an agent can read (heuristic 11, SPOT) and the file an agent is pointed at does not let it understand the lane it is standing in (heuristic 13, files make internal sense in isolation). The cost is wasted probes; no wrong change was observed to follow. Whether the lane creator omits the files is not verifiable from this tree.

In these sessions the agent placed literal envelope markup such as </rationale> inside string-valued tool fields, and the receiving MCP server rejected the call with error_type mcp_markup_detected; in several sessions the identical payload was resubmitted more than once before the agent changed course. The boundary is doing what heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings, asks: markup is refused rather than parsed out of a field value. The repeated identical resubmission is the part worth weighing under heuristic 10, clear invariants informatively enforced: the rejection names the invariant, yet the agent's next move did not change, which suggests the message does not tell the agent what to alter. The guard and its allow_mcp_markup override live in the plan-tools and fused-memory servers, not in this tree, so nothing here produces or fails to catch the behaviour.

Ops sessions running from the reify checkout invoked the escalation-watcher skill, which resolves watcher-rearm.sh through an implicit host context (DARK_FACTORY_ROOT or a dark-factory working directory); from reify the resolution failed with 'DARK_FACTORY_ROOT must be set to a valid directory' (exit 2) or the invocation ran into the ceiling timeout (exit 124), and after an exit 124 the agent re-issued the identical command rather than checking rotation limits. No file under reify's .claude/skills, scripts or docs names watcher-rearm.sh or DARK_FACTORY_ROOT, so the skill's behaviour cannot be understood from anything this tree holds (heuristic 13, files make internal sense in isolation), and the script's location is reached by ambient environment rather than by a path the skill states in one place (heuristic 11, SPOT). The fix sits in dark-factory; the exit-124 cause was not checked against any file here.

It returned parked tasks to pending even though their escalations were still open, so they became dispatchable. Nothing built on the unruled designs only by luck. The nightly legibility trickle copies agent transcript text into cause and evidence_quote fields of docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml. Any test path quoted in a sighting about missing paths is stale by construction, so it cannot be repointed without falsifying the record. tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh is a one-directional ratchet that fails on any unresolved citation not in cited-test-path-baseline.manifest. The trickle neither validates nor grandfathers new rows, so the unattended commit blocked every full-gate merge for hours. Auto-grandfathering would fight the baseline burn-down in task 7597. Verifier: The failure described no longer exists in the current tree. `tests/infra/cited-test-path-lib.sh::cited_test_path_exclusions` now excludes `docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml` from the cited-test-path scan. `tests/infra/test_cited_test_paths_resolve.sh` has a fixture (assertion E) that proves the exclusion. `docs/legibility/landing-contract.md` documents the trickle's failure class and the codebook-exempt gate charter. A new trickle row quoting a stale test path can therefore no longer redden the ratchet or block merges, and no baseline grandfathering is needed. I did not run the gate.

Unlike GNU grep, git grep requires options such as -A/-B/-C before the pattern. When -A30 follows the pattern, git treats it as a revision argument and fails with 'unable to resolve revision', exit 128. The agent writes the grep -A idiom from habit, and the exit-128 revision error looks unrelated to flag order. Verifier: The cluster describes git's own argument handling combined with an agent habit, and it is not an observable fact about the current state of /home/leo/src/reify. That guidance does not suggest putting -A after the pattern. I could not reproduce the exit-128 error with the read-only tools I have, so the claim rests on the one quoted sighting.

EOF`) semantics inside a `$(cat <<'EOF' ...)` substitution used to build a multi-line commit message.
